subject: Client load-test execution plan, IP allowlist & test creds
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Samir Reddy <samir@olive-systems.com>, Lena O'Connor <lena@olive-systems.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 7 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + proposed execution window for client-led load test

Thanks again for the call this morning — good alignment on performance targets and the general approach. Quick recap and concrete asks so we can run the customer-led load test next week: 

Key SLOs Olive cares about
- p95 generation latency <= 250ms for representative 256-token requests (single-turn)
- sustained throughput target: 400 req/s for steady-state; peak step to 1,200 req/s (ramp plan below)
- sustained concurrent streaming sessions: ~600 concurrent SSE streams
- streaming tail (time-to-first-token) target: < 120ms

Test plan (customer-led)
- You run k6/Locust from your environment using the scripts we'll share.
- Redwood will provide a dedicated test API key, a short-lived test account, and an IP allowlist.
- Proposed test window: Mar 15, 2027 02:00–06:00 UTC (we can move +/- one day if needed).
- Ramp schedule (example): 10m warmup at 50 req/s; 45m steady at 400 req/s; 15m step to 1,200 req/s; cool down. We'll confirm final timings.

Action items for Olive
- Confirm final test window (date/time) and test origin IP ranges.
- Choose k6 or Locust scenario(s) you want us to prioritize (we included both scripts).
- Share any special prompt sets or max-token configurations you'll run.

Action items for Redwood (we own these)
- Provision test API key + short-lived credentials and send IP allowlist entries.
- Enable audit-logging for the test account and ensure model fallback policy is in place.
- Provide small guidance doc on streaming (SSE vs chunked HTTP) and backpressure handling.

Attachments we plan to send: k6-script-v1.js, locustfile.py, sample ramp plan.

Ben
Ben Carter | Enterprise Solutions 
Redwood Inference

From: Samir Reddy <samir@olive-systems.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Lena O'Connor <lena@olive-systems.com>
Date: Sun, 7 Mar 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + proposed execution window for client-led load test

Thanks Ben — this looks good and mirrors what we need to validate. Couple clarifications from our side: 

1) We'll run Locust as our primary harness (we have an existing cluster in us-west-2). Can you confirm the expected connection pattern for streaming calls? Do you support both SSE and WebSocket-based streaming for the endpoints in the test account?
2) For the peak step (1,200 req/s), we may need a slightly longer ramp (30m) to hit higher concurrency safely.
3) Please send the test API key and a list of CIDRs to add to our firewall so we can originate the traffic from the right egress.

Also — can you confirm whether markdown-function or structured output tests are required, or can we stick to simple text generation for the first run?

Samir
Samir Reddy | Head of Platform Engineering
Olive Systems

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Samir Reddy <samir@olive-systems.com>, Lena O'Connor <lena@olive-systems.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Mar 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + proposed execution window for client-led load test

Samir — good questions. Quick answers and the artifacts attached. See inline: 

- Streaming: the hosted API supports SSE (server-sent events) and HTTP chunked streaming for gen endpoints; we do not expect you to run WebSocket for this test. Time-to-first-token should be comparable for SSE and chunked. I've annotated the k6 script to demonstrate streaming checks.

- Ramp: happy to use a 30m ramp for the peak step — update: warmup 15m, steady 45m, 30m ramp to peak, 20m peak hold, cool down. We'll work with you on exact durations.

- Test credentials: attached test-credentials-olive.txt (short-lived API key, expires 72h after issue).

- IP allowlist: please add the following Redwood egress CIDRs to your allowlist so our test traffic from your k6/locust orchestrator isn't blocked (we will also whitelist the test key on our side):
  - 34.201.120.0/22
  - 34.202.64.0/20
  - 54.172.0.0/18
(If you cannot accept these exact CIDRs, tell us the specific ranges from your VPC and we can provide alternate endpoints.)

- Scripts attached: k6-script-v1.js (includes streaming checks + assertions for first-token latency), locustfile.py (multiple user classes + ramp plan).

Notes on test model and fallback
- We'll provision the test account to hit model: redwood/gpt-infer-8k-v2 (quantized). For peak safety, we will configure automatic fallback to redwood/gpt-infer-4k if the host pool signals pressure. We'll also enable prefix caching for repeated warmup prompts.

Next steps: Ben to create test creds + post the Doc link to the orchestration runbook; Olive to confirm window and start times.

Ben

[attachment: k6-script-v1.js]
[attachment: locustfile.py]
[attachment: test-credentials-olive.txt]

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Reddy <samir@olive-systems.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Mar 2027 12:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Client load-test execution plan, IP allowlist & test creds

Looping in a couple of security quick checks before we hand over creds into production-sim test: 

- Keys: please ensure the test API key is issued as "ephemeral" and scoped only to the test model with a 72-hour TTL. Confirm key id and expiration in the creds file.
- Audit logs: enable full request/response logging for the test account and retain for 30 days (we will provide a download link post-test).
- Data handling: confirm that Olive will not persist any generated outputs beyond transient logs for analysis — we need a short AUP sign-off for the engagement.

Samir — can you confirm the names/emails of the runbook reviewers who will have access to logs post-test? We will only grant access to named individuals.

Neha Kapoor
Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Samir Reddy <samir@olive-systems.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Lena O'Connor <lena@olive-systems.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Mar 2027 09:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Client load-test execution plan, IP allowlist & test creds

Thanks Neha — we agree to the AUP conditions and will not persist model outputs beyond the test logs. Reviewers for access to logs: 
- Lena O'Connor (lena@olive-systems.com)
- Diego Alvarez (diego.alvarez@olive-systems.com) — will act as runbook owner during the test window

Confirming: we will run Locust-based scenarios with the updated ramp plan and aim for the peak hold at 1,200 req/s. Test window confirmed: Mar 15, 2027 02:00–06:00 UTC. We will share the exact Locust cluster IDs and runner IPs 48h before the test.

One last ask: what throttling/backoff behavior should our harness expect from the Redwood endpoint if we hit a short-lived overload? Will we receive 429s with Retry-After, or will Redwood gracefully queue/retry at the model routing layer?

Samir

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Samir Reddy <samir@olive-systems.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Mar 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Client load-test execution plan, IP allowlist & test creds

Samir — great, thanks for the confirmation and reviewers list. Final clarifications before we lock the window: 

Throttling behavior
- Primary behavior: short-lived overloads will surface 429 responses with a Retry-After header. Our routing layer will also attempt fast model fallback (to a compatible lower-capacity variant) for a subset of requests to reduce visible failures. For testing, please treat 429 as expected at the peak step and implement Retry-After respecting exponential backoff.

Pre-test deliverables (we will send these by EOD tomorrow):
- Test credentials (test-credentials-olive.txt) — expires 72h after creation.
- A small runbook with the exact ramp timeline, API endpoints, and cURL examples for streaming.
- IP allowlist confirmation (we will provision the outbound CIDRs on our side: same list we provided earlier).

Fallback & observability
- If we detect high error rates, Redwood will automatically route to a fallback variant and flag the run in the Console under the "Performance Tests" tag. We'll give you a live dashboard link during the window.

See HubSpot for the deal record and the Drive folder for scripts & runbook: https://hubspot.company/contacts/HS-78234 and https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C4D5E

If everything looks good on your end, we will provision creds and lock Mar 15 02:00–06:00 UTC as the run window.

Ben
Ben Carter | Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
